featureRef: 4.19 Accounting vouchers for money in and out
name: Record a movement as a voucher, approved by a chain that matches its size, and paid separately
priorityReason: The manual door into the ledger. Every movement the fee system has no route for arrives through here.

goal.capability: to record a cash movement, expense or refund as a formal entry through an approval chain that matches its size
goal.outcome: money moves only with the right person's authority, and approving a payment is never the same act as making it

secondaryActors.involvement: Approves vouchers at or above the lower threshold.
Sets both thresholds and approves vouchers at or above the higher one.

additional.description: A refund is approved and needs a payment voucher, which is the existing route for money leaving.
Withholding tax is deposited and the payment is recorded as a voucher.

preconditions.condition: A chart of accounts exists with the accounts to debit and credit. No feature creates it, and this cannot work without it (BR-2).

establishedBy.name: Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

preconditions.condition: Both approval thresholds are set by the Principal. They are not settable by the School Admin they constrain (BR-4).
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Accounts, School Admin or Principal.
Where a budget line applies, the budget for the period has been approved.

postConditions: The voucher exists with its amount, its two accounts, its date and its description, entered once rather than twice.
It has passed the approval chain its amount required, and no higher approval was bypassed.
On final approval it has posted to the ledger and created a payable, since the school now owes the money.
The printed voucher is the authorisation to release the money, not a second record for somebody to key back in.
An approved but unpaid voucher stays visible as a liability, so the school's commitments are not hidden until they are paid.
The later payment has discharged the payable and posted the cash movement, and the two are separate acts by separate people.
Where a budget line applies, the remaining balance was checked and an excess was pushed to the next approval level rather than blocked.
Nothing was posted without approval, and no voucher below the lower threshold waited on an approver it did not need.

businessRules.rule: A voucher is entered once, not twice. Both sides of the movement are captured in a single entry.
The accounts to debit and credit come from the chart of accounts. No feature in this document creates one, and this use case cannot work without it.

The approval required is derived from the amount and the two thresholds. Below the lower threshold the voucher posts directly, so small purchases do not wait on an approver. At or above the lower threshold the School Admin approves it; at or above the higher threshold the Principal does.
Both thresholds are set by the Principal, not the School Admin. A limit should not be settable by the person it constrains.
The voucher reaches the ledger only on final approval. A draft or a voucher awaiting approval posts nothing.
The debit and credit accounts must differ, and the two sides must total the same. A voucher that does not balance is not posted.
Approval creates a payable, since the school now owes the money. The printed voucher is the authorisation to release it rather than a second record to key back in.
The later payment discharges the payable and posts the cash movement. Approving a payment and making it are separate acts, so an approved but unpaid voucher stays visible as a liability.

Where a budget line exists the remaining balance is checked at entry, and an excess is flagged and pushed to the next approval level up. It is never blocked outright, because blocking routine spending stalls the office.
Accounts cannot approve a voucher above the lower threshold, including one they created. Creating and authorising are separate hands.
A posted voucher is never edited or deleted. A correction is a further voucher, so the ledger reads as a history.
A voucher carries its supporting document where one exists. A payment with no bill behind it is the thing an auditor asks about.
The voucher date is when the movement occurred, and must fall in an open period. A movement cannot be posted into a closed one.

The payment is recorded, discharging the payable (BR-8).

basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval, or routes it up to the Principal where the amount or a budget excess requires it.

basicFlow.userAction: Approves the voucher at or above the higher threshold.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Posts the entry to the ledger and creates the payable, since the school now owes the money.

alternateFlows.condition: The amount is below the lower threshold
alternateFlows.behaviour: The voucher posts directly with no approver, so a small purchase does not wait on somebody's inbox (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The voucher would exceed its budget line
alternateFlows.navigation: Create voucher → Budget line → Awaiting Principal
alternateFlows.behaviour: The excess is flagged and the voucher is pushed to the next approval level up. It is never blocked outright, because blocking routine spending stalls the office (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The approver does not accept the voucher
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts with a written reason. Nothing has posted and the money has not moved.

alternateFlows.condition: The voucher is approved but not yet paid
alternateFlows.behaviour: It stays visible as a liability with its age, so the school's commitments are not hidden until they are paid (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The voucher is a refund of an unused credit
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Fee → Refunds → Approve → Finance → Vouchers
alternateFlows.behaviour: The refund raises a payment voucher through this route. No separate mechanism exists for money leaving the school.
alternateFlows.function: createVoucher('Payment voucher', amount, debitAccount, creditAccount, date, description)

alternateFlows.condition: A posted voucher is found to be wrong
alternateFlows.behaviour: A further voucher corrects it. The posted one is never edited or deleted, so the ledger reads as a history (BR-11).
alternateFlows.function: createVoucher(type, amount, debitAccount, creditAccount, date, description)

departures.requirement: Approving a voucher and recording its payment are distinct acts, and an approved unpaid voucher is visible as a liability throughout.
The approval required is derived from the amount and cannot be chosen, lowered or bypassed by the person submitting.
A posted voucher is never edited or deleted. Corrections are further vouchers.
A budget excess escalates the approval but never prevents the voucher, because routine spending must not stall.
Vouchers, approvals and supporting documents are retained 7 years as financial records.

openQuestions.question: What are the two approval thresholds?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The Principal sets them, but no starting values are given.

openQuestions.question: Who creates and maintains the chart of accounts? No feature in the document does.
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Nothing financial can be built without it.

openQuestions.question: Should a voucher below the lower threshold still require a supporting document?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and a small cash payment with no bill is where leakage starts.

openQuestions.question: Who may record the payment against an approved voucher — the same person who created it?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and it is the last point at which separation of duty matters.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: attachments
conventionsApplied.rule: Uploaded files are limited to 10 MB and to PDF, JPG, PNG, DOCX and XLSX unless a use case states otherwise. File type is validated by content, not by extension.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
